requestLimits.title: Request size
requestLimits.description: Limits on what each request to the AI provider may use. Leave a field empty for no limit. Sizes are estimates: characters divided by 4.
requestLimits.budgetHint: The largest request to send. Older turns are left out to fit, and a message that still cannot fit stops with a message instead of reaching the provider. Set it under your provider's per-request or per-minute token limit; the system prompt and tool descriptions alone can be about 8,000.
requestLimits.outputHint: The most tokens one answer may use. A lower cap keeps answers shorter, but a long report can be cut off.
requestLimits.outOfRange: Enter a whole number from {{min}} to {{max}}, or leave it empty.
requestLimits.summariesHint: When a chat grows long (three quarters of the request budget, or 20,000 tokens without one), the model summarizes its earlier turns and later requests carry the summary instead. Each summary is one more request to the AI provider, masked like your messages, and some detail of the earlier turns is lost. Off by default.

rules.assumption: Each rule is shown as Apty's DOM Settings editor holds it: Attribute Name rows test the attribute's name, Attribute Value rows the value of the attribute they name, and Apty ignores a value when any row matches. aiProvider.label: AI provider
aiProvider.notConfigured: No API key or model is set.
aiProvider.notConfiguredFix: Open Settings → AI Configuration, enter the API key and a model for your provider, turn it on and click Save Settings.
aiProvider.callsTools: {{model}} answered in {{latency}} ms and calls tools.
aiProvider.noTools: {{model}} answered in {{latency}} ms but did not call a tool. The agent needs function calling.
aiProvider.noToolsFix: Choose a model that supports function (tool) calling: in AI Configuration, Test Connection marks each model.
aiProvider.toolsUnknown: {{model}} answered in {{latency}} ms; whether it calls tools could not be determined.

aptyClient.label: Apty Client
aptyClient.notConnectedFix: Open Settings → Apty Integration, click Detect (or paste the Client's extension ID) and click Connect.
aptyClient.notInstalled: No enabled extension has the ID {{id}}.
aptyClient.notInstalledFix: Install or enable the Apty Client in chrome://extensions, or correct the ID in Apty Integration.
aptyClient.noAnswer: The Apty Client did not answer.
aptyClient.fixNoReceiver: The Apty Client does not let this extension in. Add "{{agentId}}" to externally_connectable.ids in the Client's manifest.json, reload the Client in chrome://extensions, then run the checks again.
aptyClient.fixNoResponse: The Apty Client answers but has no Agent bridge. Install the Agent bridge module in the Client's service worker (docs/integrations/apty/README.md) and reload the Client.
aptyClient.fixTimeout: The Apty Client accepted the message but never answered. Install or update the Agent bridge module in its service worker, and check chrome://extensions for errors on the Client.
aptyClient.fixSendFailed: Chrome refused to message the Apty Client. Check that the extension ID in Apty Integration is the Client's ID (32 letters a–p).
aptyClient.fixMalformed: The Apty Client's bridge module is out of date. Update it to the current contract (docs/integrations/apty/README.md).
aptyClient.noResources: The Client answers the handshake but not the request list.
aptyClient.noResourcesFix: Update the Agent bridge module in the Client: it must answer apty-debug-agent:list-observed-resources.
aptyClient.answering: Answering: status, logs and {{count}} observed request(s).

body.notObserved: The Client no longer lists this call. Load the calls again.
body.failed: The call failed, so there is no body.
body.failedWithError: The call failed, so there is no body: {{error}}
body.pending: The Client hasn't reported a response for this call yet.
body.denied: Not fetched: its URL matches "{{entry}}" in the body deny list (Settings → Data handling).

body.tooLargeToRedact: The body is {{count}} characters. Redaction takes at most 100,000 characters of text at once; a longer JSON body is redacted value by value, but this one is not JSON, has a single value over that limit, or has text that runs from one value into the next. It was withheld (not shown or kept) rather than shown partly redacted.

CNV-02.summary: No {{kind}} named “{{name}}” is published in this environment.
CNV-02.fix: Publish it to the environment the user is on, or give its exact name or sourceId.

CNV-03.fix: In Studio, clear “Hide from widget” in its settings and publish.

CNV-04.summary: This {{kind}} has no name in any language.
CNV-04.fix: Give it a name in the user's language and publish.

CNV-05.summary: The {{field}} is empty for {{languages}}, so “{{name}}” is dropped in that language.
CNV-05.fix: Add the message in that language, or turn the option off, and publish.

CNV-07.summary: Every segment that lists it ({{segments}}) is turned off, so it is hidden from everyone.
CNV-07.fix: Turn one of these segments on, or remove the item from them, and publish.

CNV-08.summary: The rules of its active segments ({{segments}}) are missing from rule.json, so they never match.
CNV-08.fix: Open each segment in Studio, save it with a rule, and publish.

CNV-13.summary: “{{name}}” has no name in {{language}} ({{code}}), so the widget drops it for {{language}} users.
CNV-13.fix: In Studio, add and publish the {{language}} translation: its name, and the success and feedback messages if they are on.

WNV-01.summary: app-urls.json is an empty list: no application is defined, or the file failed its schema check, so Apty loads nothing on any page.
WNV-01.fix: Read its status code, then the Console for “Error fetching data” or “Error parsing response”. If one entry is malformed, fix it in Admin and publish.

WNV-02.summary: No environment's URL pattern matches this page, so nothing from Apty loads here.
WNV-02.fix: In Admin, add the exact host users open (with or without www) to the right environment's URLs, publish and reload. With the Console set to Verbose, “No active application found” confirms it.

WNV-03.summary: {{envs}} has a URL pattern for this site that does not cover this page, so no content runs here.
WNV-03.fix: In Admin, set the environment's URL to the application's base URL (a * covers every page under it), publish and reload. Change a test environment first if there is one.

WNV-07.summary: The widget is limited to segments that can never be active here ({{segments}}), and the option for other users is off: nobody sees it.
WNV-07.fix: In Admin, under “TARGET AUDIENCE”, turn one of the widget's segments on or fix its rule, or enable the widget for all users. Publish and reload.

WNV-07-noneChosen.summary: The widget is set to show only to specific segments, but none is chosen, and the option for other users is off: nobody sees it.
WNV-07-noneChosen.fix: In Admin, under “TARGET AUDIENCE”, choose the widget's segments or enable the widget for all users. Publish and reload.

LOG-01.summary: Apty found no environment whose URL pattern matches the page, so nothing loads there.
LOG-01.fix: Ask “the widget is not appearing” in the tab of that page to see which pattern misses it, then add the page's host to the right environment in Admin and publish.

LOG-02.summary: A content file failed to load or failed its schema check, and Apty then treats it as empty.
LOG-02.fix: Read that file's status code next; if one entry is malformed, fix it in Admin and publish.

LOG-03.summary: The injected loader found no environment for this URL: this is URL matching, not whitelisting.
LOG-03.fix: Check the environments' URL patterns (ask “the widget is not appearing” here), and that the matching environment has a client version for Injected mode.

LOG-04.summary: The page's Content Security Policy blocked {{count}} load(s) from Apty's hosts ({{directives}}).
LOG-04.fix: Whitelist the Apty domains in the application's CSP. If the Console text mentions a nonce, the player needs a version with nonce support: contact support.

LOG-05.summary: The Apty Client's request for {{files}} failed, so the content in it does not reach the player.
LOG-05.fix: Fix the failing request first: a 401 or 403 points to access, a 404 to content not published to this environment, a net:: error to the network or a blocked domain.

LOG-06.summary: {{count}} resource(s) from Apty's hosts failed to load in the page.
LOG-06.fix: Ask the customer to whitelist the Apty CDN domains in their network or CSP policy, then reload.

SEL-02.summary: {{where}} is identified by {{type}}, but its {{field}} is empty, so there is nothing to look up; a filled field of another type is ignored.
SEL-02.fix: In Studio, select the element again, or fill the selector of the active identification type, then publish.

SEL-04.summary: {{where}}: the stored selector does not parse, so the lookup finds nothing.
SEL-04.fix: Select the element again in Studio, or correct the selector, then publish and reload.

SEL-05.summary: {{where}}: the selector matches nothing in the page itself but {{count}} element(s) inside a frame, and its frame path is empty, as a hand-written selector's is.
SEL-05.fix: Delete the hand-written selector and select the element with Studio's picker while inside the frame, so the frame path is recorded; then publish.

SEL-06.summary: {{where}}: the selector matches {{count}} element(s) inside a shadow root, but no shadow host is stored, so a lookup in the document never reaches them.
SEL-06.fix: Select the element again in Studio so the identification includes the shadow host chain, then publish.

SEL-07.summary: {{where}}: the stored selector matches nothing on this page.
SEL-07.fix: Look in Elements for the element nearby: it may have been renamed or moved. Select it again in Studio, then publish and reload.

SEL-08.summary: {{where}}: the selector matches {{count}} elements ({{rendered}} rendered). Apty takes the first rendered one, which may not be yours.
SEL-08.fix: Refine the selector in Studio so it matches only the intended element, then publish and reload.

SEL-09.summary: {{where}}: the selector matches one element, but it is not rendered (hidden by CSS or not displayed), so there is nothing to attach to.
SEL-09.fix: Find out why the element is hidden when the content should show: it may need a click, a tab or a scroll first.

SEL-10.summary: {{where}}: the selector matches one rendered element, but it is outside the visible part of the page.
SEL-10.fix: Scroll the element into view first, or add a scroll before the step as the KB card describes.

SEL-11.summary: {{where}}: the selector holds {{count}} generated-looking value(s), which often change after a reload.
SEL-11.fix: In Admin, Application, DOM Analysis, add an ignore rule for the attribute that changes, select the element again in Studio and publish.

SEL-12.summary: {{where}}: its frame path names {{depth}} frame level(s), but the element is at depth {{found}}.
SEL-12.fix: Select the element again in Studio inside the frame that holds it, so the frame path matches the live nesting; then publish.

SEL-12-otherFrame.summary: {{where}}: matches nothing in the frame its frame path leads to, but {{count}} element(s) in another frame at the same level.
SEL-12-otherFrame.fix: Select the element again in Studio inside the frame that holds it, so the frame path points at that frame; then publish.

SEL-13.summary: {{where}}: shadow host selector {{index}} of {{total}} finds no open shadow root, so the lookup falls back to the document and finds nothing.
SEL-13.fix: Select the element again in Studio so its shadow host chain is recorded, then publish.

DOM-01.summary: {{count}} of {{total}} frames could not be inspected (often a cross-origin frame), so Apty's selection there was not checked.
DOM-01.fix: Make sure the frame that holds the element is registered for Apty, and select the element inside that frame in Studio.

DOM-03.summary: {{count}} list(s) draw only the rows in view ({{drawn}} drawn now), so a target further down is not in the page until it is scrolled to.
DOM-03.fix: Scroll the row into view before the step, as the KB card describes; a selector cannot find a row that is not drawn.

DOM-04.summary: Some interactive elements are covered, zero-sized or outside the view where a click would land; {{overlays}} element(s) sit at a very high z-index.
DOM-04.fix: Find what covers the element (a sticky header, a dialog, a chat launcher) and test with it closed; Apty's content can be hidden behind it too.

DOM-05.summary: {{count}} element(s) share their id with another in the same document or shadow root, so a selector on that id matches more than one.
DOM-05.fix: Do not select these elements by id: refine the selector in Studio with another attribute, then publish.

DOM-06.summary: {{percent}}% of the interactive elements analyzed have no unique, stable selector by Apty's own rules and would need a hand-made one.
DOM-06.fix: For the elements your content uses, check the selector Studio recorded and make it stable (Ignore and Partial Selector rules, or XPath), then publish.

DOM-06-ambiguous.summary: {{ambiguous}} of {{total}} interactive elements analyzed only have selectors that match several elements, and {{wrongTarget}} have one that picks the wrong element.
DOM-06-ambiguous.fix: For the elements your content uses, refine the selector in Studio so it matches only the intended element (a stable attribute, or Ignore and Partial Selector rules), then publish.

DOM-07.summary: {{count}} of {{total}} frames can only be told apart by position or by their address, so a stored frame path can point at another frame.
DOM-07.fix: Give each frame a stable id or name, or add a Partial Selector rule for its address, then select the element again.

DAP-01.summary: The AI assistant is turned off for this application, so the widget shows no chat.
DAP-01.fix: Turn the AI assistant on in the application's widget settings in Admin, then publish.

DAP-02.summary: The newest chat call failed before ai-service answered ({{detail}}).
DAP-02.fix: In Injected mode this is most often the CORS check (see the origin check); otherwise the network or a blocker extension. Ask again with the Network tab open.

DAP-03.summary: The newest chat call failed with HTTP {{httpStatus}}, so Dapty could not answer.
DAP-03.fix: A 4xx means ai-service rejected the request; a 5xx means it failed while answering. Send the time of the call and the status to Apty support.

DAP-03-panel.summary: The chat panel shows an error instead of an answer to the last question.
DAP-03-panel.fix: Open the Network tab, ask again and read the widget chat call's status.

DAP-04.summary: The page's origin is not among the origins the application's {{urls}} environment URL(s) allow, so in Injected mode ai-service's CORS check rejects the chat call.
DAP-04.fix: Add this page's address, with its https:// scheme, to an environment's URLs in Admin, then publish. ai-service reads them from app-urls.json, cached for up to 5 minutes.

DAP-04-noScheme.summary: The page's origin is not among the origins the application's environment URLs allow, and {{withoutScheme}} of its {{urls}} URL(s) have no https:// scheme, which allows no origin. In Injected mode ai-service's CORS check rejects the chat call.

DAP-05.summary: Dapty gave its fixed “couldn't find information” reply: no indexed document or allowed web page answered the question.
DAP-05.fix: Check that this application has documents or a connected repository indexed in Admin (AI settings), that they cover the question, and that the application's support docs domains list your help site.

DAP-06.summary: Dapty suggested “{{name}}”, which this environment does not publish, so clicking it opens nothing.
DAP-06.fix: Dapty lists the environment's items from ai-service's own copy of the content files, which can lag a publish by a few minutes, or the model named an item it was not given. Publish the item to this environment, or ask again once ai-service has the newest content.

next.fixConnection: Fix the connection to the Apty Client first; this says nothing about the content.
next.reload: Reload the problem page, then ask again.
next.readStatus: An empty list has several causes: read its status code and the Console next.
next.waitForLoad: Wait for the page to finish loading, then ask again.
next.denyList: Remove the entry from Settings, Data handling, to let this file be checked.
next.bodyLimit: The Apty Client did not keep this file. Reload and ask again, or paste the file.
next.openResponse: Open the response and see what the server returned.
next.manual4x: Use the manual paste path for 4.x.
next.nameItem: Name the one that is missing to check it in full.
next.whichOne: Which one? Give the full name or the sourceId.
next.testAsMember: Test as a user known to match the segment, and confirm the widget shows for that user.
next.openItems: Then look at the open checks below; the files cannot decide them.
next.sendSupport: Send support the Apty version, the environment, the sourceId, a screenshot of the open widget and the trimmed entry.
next.openAppPage: Open the application page where the widget is missing in this tab, then ask again.
next.comparePatterns: Compare the URL patterns of the environments that match this page in Admin; make the one that should not win more specific.
next.removalTest: Disable or remove Apty and repeat the exact flow: if the same 404s still occur, they are not Apty's.
next.readConsoleText: Read the exact CSP text in the Console: a nonce means a player version with nonce support, a plain block means whitelisting.
next.runInConsole: Run the item's jQuery or custom-script selector in the Console on this page and see whether it returns the intended element.
next.openItemPage: Open the page where the content should show in this tab, then ask again.
next.reloadAndRetest: Reload the page and ask again: a selector holding a generated value often stops matching after a reload.
next.playWorkflow: Play the workflow once in this tab, so the Apty Client loads its steps, then ask again.
next.nameStep: Name the step that fails (“step 3”), with the page where it fails open in this tab.
next.checkTiming: Check that the element is there when the content runs (Apty retries once a second for 5 seconds), and that the item is published here and its segment matches.
next.askDapty: Open the widget's Ask Dapty chat on the page in this tab, ask the question again, then check again.
next.checkKb: Check what this application's AI knowledge holds in Admin (documents and connected repositories), and whether it covers the question.
next.clickAsUser: Ask Dapty again as the user, on the page where the item's visibility rule should pass, and click the suggestion.

notChecked.cors: CORS blocks, which the browser does not report to the page

notChecked.closed-shadow-roots: Elements inside closed shadow roots, which neither Apty nor the agent can open
notChecked.canvas: Content drawn on a canvas, which has no elements to select
notChecked.kb-contents: What the indexed documents say, which only ai-service can search
notChecked.suggestion-ids: The suggestions' ids, which the chat panel does not show, so they were matched by name

harCheck.intro: Run the visibility checks on a HAR file a customer recorded, when their Apty Client cannot be connected.
harCheck.privacy: The file is read in this panel only. It is not stored or sent; its Apty files go through the deny list and redaction before any check.
harCheck.noAptyFiles: No Apty content files in this HAR
harCheck.noAptyFilesHelp: Record it again with the widget open and Preserve log on. In Extension mode, export the HAR from the Apty Client's service worker in chrome://extensions, where its calls are made.
harCheck.noFileInCalls: Apty's calls in this HAR brought no file
harCheck.noFileInCallsHelp: {{count}} call(s) for Apty content failed or were recorded without a body. A check names each file's status; record again with Preserve log on and reload the page, so the calls finish.
harCheck.environments: This HAR holds calls from {{count}} Apty environments; the checks read the newest one's files.
harCheck.version4x: This HAR holds 4.x content files; the checks are verified for 5.x only.
